description: A wav sample player with cue and loop cursors, a four-stage envelope, reverse and ping-pong playback, and polyphonic pitch tracking

notes: nothing plays until a sample is loaded: right-click the panel and use Load Sample, or right-click the waveform display.
the PLAY and STOP buttons act on the first channel of polyphony only.
the waveform display shows the file name, its length and its channel count, and carries its own right-click menu with the cursor and preset commands on it.
menu: Load Sample — opens a file chooser for the sample this module plays
Select Samples Root — picks a folder, after which a Samples Browser submenu appears for loading
Interpolation: None, Linear 1, Linear 2, Hermite — chooses how the sample is read between points, which matters when the file's sample rate differs from Rack's or the tuning is not zero
Anti-aliasing filter — adds two-times oversampling and a 20kHz lowpass before the outputs
Phase scan — moves the cue and loop cursors to the nearest zero crossings, which stops loop clicks; it should be off for one-cycle waveforms
Polyphonic OUTs — carries the V/Oct polyphony through to the outputs; with it off every voice is summed into single-channel outputs
Polyphonic Master IN — lets the MASTER CV jack take a polyphonic cable matching the V/Oct channels, for per-voice velocity
EOC pulse from — a submenu of eight points, each ticked or not, at which the EOC output sends a pulse: TRG/GATE (stop), STOP trig, CUE END, CUE START, LOOP END, LOOP START, PING and PONG
Reset cursors on Load — puts the cue and loop cursors back to 0% and 100% whenever a new sample is loaded
Disable NAV Buttons — stops the panel navigation buttons from loading anything, so they cannot be pressed by accident
Store Sample in Patch — saves the loaded sample inside the patch file, which can make it very large
Unlimited Sample Size (risky) — lifts the memory ceiling on the loaded sample, at the risk of a crash on a file the machine cannot hold
Presets: Wavetable, Triggered Sample with Envelope, Drum Player — sets the cursors, mode and envelope in one go for one of three common uses
